To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression levels of a number of genes are altered in gastric cancer and these changes are associated with copy number alterations.

integrated gene expression and gene copy number microarray analyses of gastric tumors and cell lines highlighted 13 genes with altered expression levels and copy numbers, and that these 13 genes may be useful for the early diagnosis of gastric cancer.
we have identified genes that are differentially expressed and copy number altered in gastric tumors and gastric cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets for gastric cancer.

the discovery and characterization of genes that are involved in the development of primary gastric tumors, and the results provide a basis for further studies on the role of these candidate genes in gastric carcinogenesis.
the development of novel biomarkers for gastric carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genes highlighted in this study may be of biological and clinical importance in the development of primary gastric tumors.
these genes are associated with gastric carcinogenesis.
the genes identified in this study may be important for gastric carcinomas and that the expression of these genes may serve as a biomarker for this cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integrated analysis of copy number and expression levels in gastric cancer revealed several genes that may have important roles in the development of this disease.

the expression of these genes can be regulated by copy number changes and that they are differentially expressed in gastric tumors compared to nonmalignant tissue, and therefore, they are potential biomarkers for the diagnosis, prognosis and treatment of gastric cancer.
the expression levels of ALPK2, CEACAM6, ERBB2 and OSMR are upregulated and the expression levels of ASAP1, HHIPL1, LTB4, MMP9, OSMR, PNMT and PTPRA are downregulated in gastric cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integrated microarray analysis is a powerful method to highlight genes of potential clinical importance.
integrated copy number and gene profiling can identify genes that are differentially expressed in cancerous samples and are associated with copy number alterations.
the combination of gene expression and gene copy number analysis is a very powerful tool in identifying potential biomarkers and drug targets in gastric cancer and in other types of cancer as well.
